checks.label: Each puzzle's answer is worked out from its table: 10 °C at 8 min is (8, 10); 64 ÷ 10 = 6.4, so 10 °C a square; −10 °C at 4 h is (4, −10); line B is the draining tank's best fit; a best-fit line need pass through none; the readings that bend take a smooth curve; the 10 min reading is the swapped one

A reading with its two numbers swapped is plotted somewhere else: 10 °C at 8 min swapped is (10, 8), and the cooling tank's 32 °C at 10 min swapped sits at (32, 10), more than a square and a half below the smooth curve, with no point at 10 min

Incorrectly assigning points to the axes or quadrants on the coordinate plane: the freezer's reading of −10 °C at 4 h is drawn below the time axis, and the slip that drops its minus, (4, 10), puts it above in the warning colour

Construct a best-fit straight line graph from supplied experimental data: each best-fit line the lesson draws is worked out from its readings, runs within about half a square of every one, with some above it and some below, and the line laid on the filling tank is judged the same way

Never connect even linearized data point-to-point with straight lines: the dot-to-dot zigzag is drawn only as the slip, in the warning colour, and every answer drawn through the readings is one straight best-fit line or one smooth curve

Plot ordered pairs on graph paper, either given or calculated and join the points with an appropriate curve: the readings that bend get one smooth curve that runs within a third of a square of every reading, where the best straight line misses one by a square or more

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and each wrong answer it names is the one a slip gives, shown in the warning colour: the numbers swapped, a square taken as 1, a minus dropped, a scale that overflows or squashes, a line with every reading on one side or too flat, a zigzag, the ends forced, a straight line through a bend

Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away: the readout says (?, ?), the side has no numbers until a scale is picked, no line is singled out or drawn, the swapped point is not marked, and no reading is ringed
Every screen, finished, keeps its labels inside the picture and clear of each other and its points inside the graph, for every answer, right or wrong

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart and counted steps at least 0.2 s apart
